title: Initial Access with SAP* (Safe-Mode Scenarios)
description: These actions assume you have authenticated as the default SAP* user — typically possible in systems running in safe-mode, newly installed instances, or where SAP* protections were not correctly configured. The following TCodes can be used to pivot, escalate, or extract sensitive data.

techniques.What it do?: Used to create a new dialog user with full privileges. Essential in safe-mode as SAP* can bootstrap permanent access by creating a named user that bypasses default protections.
Allows execution of OS-level commands via configured external commands. Useful for RCE, although some restrictions apply depending on configuration (e.g., whitelisted commands).
Access the SQL editor through Diagnostics > SQL Editor. You can query internal tables like USR02 to extract usernames and password hashes.
Execute ABAP reports directly. Using the RSBDCOS0 program offers a more flexible and powerful way to execute OS commands than SM49/SM69, often with fewer restrictions.
Launches the SAP GUI for HTML. You can access the file browser component here to upload arbitrary files to the backend server, including web shells or payloads.
Allows invocation of RFC-enabled function modules. You can use modules like ARCHIVFILE_CLIENT_TO_SERVER to move uploaded files from the GUI into the SAP filesystem.
